free_tier.stated: Apache-2.0; no limit imposed by the software

egress.terms: whatever the host's NIC and the hosting bill allow

chaining: the front half of the self-hosted tunnel chain: your controller, your frontend, and then a plain VPS bill. The relay software is free and the egress is not.

evidence.proved: 'Run Zrok on your own infrastructure with no limits'
Apache-2.0 repository; docs/current/ holds the bandwidth-limit journal and relax cycle, so the hosted limits are controller policy rather than protocol

notes: The hosted limits are NetFoundry's policy; a default self-hosted controller has no bandwidth journal configured. Re-graded 2026-10-23: the software is free and the path is not, because it needs a host. The finding is the host.

extras.transit_note: the software runs on the operator's host and the bytes transit that host's NIC
extras.hosting_requirement: a rented or free compute service

interface_detail: zrok share public against your own controller
confidence_note: no probe: a self-hosted zrok controller needs an enrolment token and was not stood up
binding_note: the software imposes no byte meter; what runs out is the monthly egress allowance of the host it runs on, and that host is a separate provider
